statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Weekend venue closure leaves no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail remains far below the block threshold while Stress stays elevated on hawkish rate repricing and an escalating US-Iran tanker exchange around the Strait of Hormuz.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC futures-reopen window rather than across the session; existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: US-Iran tanker exchange widens into a thin 22:00 UTC futures reopen ahead of a US Labor Day holiday
body: CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00 UTC, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path is observable at this assessment. The last verified tape remains Friday September 4: ^NDX closed 29,544.15 (+0.21%) inside a 29,440.15-29,655.22 range, a mid-range finish with no session-extreme hold, and VIX ended at 14.53 after a 13.80-14.58 day range. The S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,718.41, the Nasdaq Composite 0.29% to 26,506.99 and the Dow 0.51% to 53,413.60 after the August employment report printed 162,000 payrolls against roughly 56,000 consensus, with prior months revised up a combined 55,000 and unemployment steady at 4.1%. That repricing lifted the implied odds of a 25bp hike at the September 15-16 FOMC to 58.4% from 49.4% a day earlier; H.15 still shows the September 3 readings of 2Y 4.34% and 10Y 4.77%. The pre-FOMC communications blackout began September 5 and runs through September 17. The second driver is energy: the US-Iran tanker exchange widened over the weekend, with US Central Command reporting three Iranian vessels struck after Iranian ballistic missiles were fired toward a US carrier and destroyer, and Iran claiming strikes on tankers and US-linked vessels. Brent settled Friday at $96.28, its highest since July 24 and up more than 9% on the week, with WTI near $91.5 and US diesel at a record $5.85 per gallon average. Reported Hormuz transits remain near 13 vessels per day. Shared delayed cross-asset context is directionally mixed rather than aligned: latest-session megacaps were 3 up and 5 down with a -1.22% mean, while all seven tracked semiconductors were higher, which reduces directional conviction rather than amplifying Tail. Because no live price path exists, no directional efficiency, shallow-pullback sequence or failed retracement can be observed, so Tail is held in the low band at 5 and the conditional risk is placed in the 22:00 UTC reopen hour, where weekend escalation would be absorbed by the thinnest order book of the week. Stress stays elevated at 56 on the unresolved rates and energy backdrop. US cash equity markets are closed on Monday September 7 for Labor Day; the next verified checkpoints are the NFIB survey on September 8, August PPI on September 10 and August CPI on September 11.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available. Tail held flat at 4-5 with EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress rose from 40 during Saturday's European hours to a 57 peak around the Saturday evening tanker exchange, then oscillated between 52 and 57 across the remaining weekend closure and finished the window back at 57. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover ten further closed hours, the 22:00 UTC futures reopen, and an Asian and European session on a US Labor Day holiday. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band except for the single reopen hour, which reaches 20 and maps to WATCH where a widening Hormuz tanker exchange meets the thinnest depth of the week, before decaying toward 8-9 as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. Stress peaks near 67 at the reopen on the combined rates and energy backdrop before unwinding toward 55. No US macro release falls inside the window, US cash equities are closed on September 7 for Labor Day and the Fed is in its pre-FOMC blackout; the next scheduled checkpoints are the NFIB survey on September 8, August PPI on September 10 and August CPI on September 11, ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC.
